youtube_title: The Lady Elgin, 1860: about 300 lost in one night on Lake Michigan
body: On September 8, 1860, the steamer Lady Elgin was carrying an estimated 400 people home from Chicago to Milwaukee, most of them Irish residents of Milwaukee's Third Ward. Around 2:30 in the morning, in high winds and heavy rain, the schooner Augusta struck her. The Lady Elgin broke up and sank in less than half an hour, miles off Winnetka, Illinois. About 300 people were lost, the captain among them. On shore, a Northwestern student named Edward Spencer pulled people from the surf; he is credited with saving 17. Milwaukee's Third Ward was devastated. The wreck was found in 1989, off Highland Park, Illinois. Counts of those aboard and lost vary by source.
